correctness.rationale: The unique inverse polynomial is Q_alpha(z)=P_X(1-1/alpha+z/alpha); because X has maximum n, any alpha>0 preimage has maximum n. Its coefficients are binom(n,k) alpha^(-n) E[W^k(alpha-W)^(n-k)]. Beta size biasing reduces each odd exponent to a Beta(A,B) shifted odd moment. An integration-by-parts Stein identity proves by induction that E[(c-V)^m]>=0 for c>=(A+m-1)/(A+B+m-1). With A=a+k and m=n-k all thresholds coincide exactly at (a+n-1)/(a+b+n-1). Even powers are nonnegative. Normalization follows from polynomial evaluation at one. The n-1 coefficient is a strictly positive factor times (alpha-rho), establishing impossibility below and a zero at rho. The exact-rational checker run from the actual standalone program passed 288 parameter cases, which are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Closest explicit mathematical predecessor is the 2022 Kella-Löpker implicit maximal-odd-root characterization and its uniform beta(1,1) example. The new claim evaluates that maximum in closed form for every positive pair of Beta shapes using a nontrivial uniform odd-moment induction. The 2023 Peyhardi and 2024 Jones articles treat convolution/quasi-Polya thinning and dual mixture closure, not minimal independent Bernoulli de-thinning of beta-binomial marginals. Accessible historical claims and targeted mathematical records did not establish equivalence or stronger coverage. Unindexed equivalent derivations remain a genuine originality risk.
residual_risks: Theorem 19 in Kella-Löpker implicitly determines this index and might be called an equivalent algorithmic characterization; the contribution is its nontrivial full Beta closed-form evaluation, not an independent general root framework.
A differently named classical result concerning beta-binomial factorial moments, absolute monotonicity, or inverse Pólya mixing could be equivalent and unindexed.
Peyhardi publisher PDF could not be fully retrieved; its accessible sections and the fully readable Jones article show distinct operator focus, but this access gap remains.
Automated semantic search ranking is not exhaustive and is not a proof of priority.

value.rationale: The beta-binomial family is the canonical finite exchangeable success-count model with heterogeneous latent Bernoulli rates. A sharp minimum independent-Bernoulli thinning scale is a natural identifiable structural invariant that tells exactly which survival probabilities admit any finite latent count. The two-real-shape, all-n closed form removes the general predecessor's nontrivial odd-polynomial root search, extends the documented uniform subcase, and supplies an explicit boundary preimage with a zero n-1 cell. The result is a complete structural classification rather than a manufactured parameter slice; no broader application theorem is asserted.
